newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Suspected explosives found before Manila APEC meet.
newsitem.headline: Suspected explosives found before Manila APEC meet.

text.p: Philippine police found suspected explosives at the Manila airport on Wednesday hours before APEC ministers were to begin arriving for a world leaders' summit, airport sources said.
Bomb disposal experts sealed off the arrival area of the airport terminal where the suspected explosives were found in an abandoned black bag and barred arriving passengers from the lobby.
"Don't come near, it's positive," a police officer whispered to reporters after he peered into the bag. military bomb experts arrived to take the suspicious objects away.
Airport general manager Francisco Atayde refused to say what the bag contained.
"When there are suspicious and unattended bags left behind, the security people have to make sure these are properly handled," Atayde said. "That is what they did."
Other airport officials downplayed the incident, dismissing it as merely a drill.
"This is just a security precaution. This is just an exercise," airport security commander Major Richard Parkon said.

An airport source who asked not to be identified said at least one of the objects in the bag was a grenade. Others said it contained suspected C-4 plastic explosive and what appeared to be blasting caps.
Bomb disposal experts wore protective heavy clothing as they retrieved the contents of the bag after ripping it open using a detonator they set off from a distance.
Foreign and trade ministers of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum were to begin arriving on Thursday for talks to prepare for the APEC summit to be held on Monday.
The ministers meeting is to be held in Manila and the summit of 18 APEC member economies at Subic Bay freeport northwest of the capital.

The Philippines has imposed very strict security measures to ensure the safety of U.S. President Bill Clinton and other APEC leaders. But officials denied there were any specific plots against any leader.

"Up to this moment, there is no confirmed information about any terrorist threat, whether local or foreign," summit organising commission head Lisandro Abadia said on Wednesday after the suspected explosives were found at the airport.
Bomb-sniffing dogs earlier on Wednesday found explosives in a building at Subic Bay, the venue of the summit, but officials also dismissed it as merely a security rehearsal.
Dozens of people evacuated the building near the gates of Subic Bay freeport four hours drive from Manila after an anonymous caller said a bomb had been planted there.

But Subic Bay Metropolitian Authority Chairman Richard Gordon told Reuters it was just a drill to test how quickly security forces would respond to an emergency and how well the dogs could detect explosives.
The explosives were packed into a pipe bomb.
"It's a drill... part of the whole she-bang so that we would be able to test the capacity of our canine dogs," he said by telephone. "It's a field training exercise."
